title: "Nonlinear - Generalized Addictive Model (GAM)"
format: 
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 3

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tumr)
```




The package also includes `gam()`, which fits a generalized additive mixed
effects model to tumor growth data. This model is useful when tumor growth
over time follows a complex nonlinear trajectory that cannot be captured by
polynomial terms.

By default, `gam()` fits the model:

$$
\log(\text{measure}) \sim \text{group} + s(\text{time},\ \text{by} = \text{group}) + (\text{time} \mid \text{id})
$$
where $s(\cdot)$ is a group-specific smooth term for time.

## Model fit
```{r}
melanoma1$months <- melanoma1$Day / (365/12)
mel1 <- tumr(melanoma1, ID, months, Volume, Treatment)
fit <- tumr_gam(mel1)
```

## Result summary
```{r}
summary(fit)
```

## Plot
```{r}
plot(mel1) 
plot(mel1) + ggplot2::scale_y_log10()
plot(fit, "predict")
plot(fit, "contrast")
```
